subject.title: fix(mcp): honor `disabled` flag to prevent spawning disabled servers

question: Should OpenClaw permanently add `disabled` as a second public MCP enablement field, or keep `enabled` canonical and handle observed `disabled` entries only through diagnostics or migration?
rationale: Accepting the branch changes the public configuration and upgrade contract, including precedence when both keys exist; repository policy and current documentation favor one canonical runtime shape, so maintainer intent is required.

options.title: Keep one canonical field
options.body: Remove the runtime/schema/type alias and, if useful, diagnose or migrate `disabled` through doctor while preserving `enabled` as the only steady-state setting.

options.title: Approve the alias contract
options.body: Keep `disabled`, but explicitly define precedence, upgrade behavior, documentation, compatibility tests, and canonical persistence before merge.

options.title: Close as redundant
options.body: Decline the alias because the supported CLI, Control UI, and config contract already provide temporary disablement through `enabled: false`.

recommendation.title: Keep one canonical field
recommendation.body: Remove the runtime/schema/type alias and, if useful, diagnose or migrate `disabled` through doctor while preserving `enabled` as the only steady-state setting.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged history defines the current MCP operator controls, canonical normalization, shared runtime merge, and documentation contract.
